name: feature-tabs
purpose: The feature walkthrough band of a product page: a horizontal section title, with its button beside the headline, over up to three tabs on one side and the active tab's media on the other. A tab's media is its own code file (a `code-block` with line numbers whose lines rise in while the tab is open, on a pixelate texture in a taller stage), the band's live scene (handed the open tab's `value`), or the tab's illustration. It is a page section — the site places it from a `{ _id: 'feature-tabs', props }` entry and binds `props` straight onto it — and it composes `section-module`, `section-title`, `frame-box`, `media-tabs`, `code-block`, `illustration`, `button`, `link` and the webkit scene assets. The tabs advance on a timer that pauses under the pointer or keyboard focus and never runs under reduced motion; that state is owned by `media-tabs`.
useWhen: Use FeatureTabs for up to three tabs beside a media on a product page.
To walk through the two or three features behind one claim, one picture at a time, like Functions' Observability.
avoidWhen: For architectures drawn as diagrams across the full width → use `architecture-tabs`.
For a scroll-driven walkthrough of more features → use `feature-scroll`.
related: media-tabs` — the timed tabs this section renders through.
illustration` — the picture a tab shows when it has no code and the band has no scene.
code-block` — the code file a tab opens as its media.
bestPractices: Keep to three tabs; tabs past the limit are not rendered.
Give every tab an `illustrationLabel` saying what its picture shows.
Use tab `code` when the feature is an API a developer reads; keep each file short enough to read in the stage. Set `copyAriaLabel` to say what the copy button copies.

Use the band `scene` when one console widget plays a different beat per tab (`{ component: 'ProductWidget', props: { name: 'functions-start' } }` with tab `value`s naming its tabs); give every tab a `value` then.

props.name: anchor
props.doc: In-page id set on the band so a `#hash` link can scroll to it.

props.name: title
props.doc: Headline of the band, rendered by the horizontal section title as its `h2`; the band renders no header when empty.

props.name: tabs
props.doc: The features, in order, at most three; each is `{ title, description, value?, code?, illustration?, illustrationLabel? }` where `value` is the stable key handed to the band scene as its `tab`, `code` is the `{ label, value, code, language?, fileName?, fileIcon? }` file the tab opens as its media, `illustration` is a registry name drawn when the tab has no code and the band no scene, and `illustrationLabel` its accessible name.

props.name: scene
props.doc: Live scene drawn as the media of every tab without code, `{ component, props? }` naming a webkit scene asset; it receives the tab's `value` as `tab` and whether the tab is open as `active`. Wins over the illustrations.

props.name: autoplay
props.doc: Opens the next tab on a timer, with the composed tabs' visible pause control.

props.name: autoplayInterval
props.doc: Milliseconds each tab holds before the next one opens.

props.name: copyAriaLabel
props.doc: Accessible name of the copy button on each tab's code file; empty keeps the code block's own.

props.name: primaryAction
props.doc: Button in the section title, beside the headline (under the frame when the band has no title); `{ label, href, trailing?, target? }` where `trailing` adds the chevron. Omitted when absent.

examples.name: Default
examples.sfc:
<script setup>
  import FeatureTabs from '@aziontech/webkit/feature-tabs'

  const tabs = [
    {
      title: 'Trace',
      description:
        'The run as a waterfall: each step placed against the invocation it belongs to, nested where it nested.',
      illustration: 'live-debugging',
      illustrationLabel: 'A trace waterfall of one invocation'
    },
    {
      title: 'Logs',
      description:
        'Structured output on the same clock as the trace, filtered by level, searchable in place.',
      illustration: 'traffic-and-cost-bar-chart',
      illustrationLabel: 'Structured logs filtered by level'
    },
    {
      title: 'Request path',
      description:
        'The workload, application, function and connector it travelled, each captioned with the time spent there.',
      illustration: 'distributed-apis',
      illustrationLabel: 'The path a request took through the platform'
    }
  ]

  const primaryAction = {
    label: 'Open an invocation',
    href: '/product-preview',
    trailing: true
  }
</script>

<template>
  <FeatureTabs
    eyebrow="Observability"
    title="Inspect every run end-to-end"
    description="Every invocation of a function is traced on the platform itself — spans, logs and the path the request took. Nothing to configure, no storage to attach. Pick a document to open it."
    :tabs="tabs"
    :primary-action="primaryAction"
  />
</template>

examples.name: Code
examples.sfc:
<script setup>
  import FeatureTabs from '@aziontech/webkit/feature-tabs'

  const file = (value, fileName, code) => ({
    label: fileName,
    value,
    language: 'javascript',
    code,
    fileName,
    fileIcon: 'ai-color ai-javascript'
  })

  const tabs = [
    {
      value: 'config',
      title: 'Declare the workload in code',
      description:
        'The hostname, the build preset and the routing live in the repository, so shipping a change is a commit rather than a console session.',
      code: file(
        'config',
        'azion.config.js',
        `export default {
  build: { preset: 'vue' },
  rules: {
    request: [
      {
        name: 'Deliver Static Assets',
        match: '.(css|js|svg|png|webp|woff2)$',
        behavior: {
          setOrigin: { name: 'origin-storage-default' },
          deliver: true
        }
      }
    ]
  }
}`
      )
    },
    {
      value: 'handler',
      title: 'Answer the request yourself',
      description:
        'Return a response from the handler when a route needs logic — an auth check, a redirect, a shaped payload — instead of sending it to the origin.',
      code: file(
        'handler',
        'main.js',
        `export default {
  async fetch(request) {
    const url = new URL(request.url)

    if (url.pathname === '/api/status') {
      return Response.json({ region: 'edge', ok: true })
    }

    return fetch(request)
  }
}`
      )
    },
    {
      value: 'storage',
      title: 'Serve objects from storage',
      description:
        'Bind a bucket to the workload and let it answer with the object directly, with no server in front of it and no egress charge behind it.',
      code: file(
        'storage',
        'assets.js',
        `export default {
  async fetch(request) {
    const url = new URL(request.url)
    const asset = await fetch(new URL(url.pathname, 'file://site-assets/'))

    return new Response(asset.body, {
      headers: { 'cache-control': 'public, max-age=86400' }
    })
  }
}`
      )
    }
  ]
</script>

<template>
  <FeatureTabs
    title="From a hostname to a full stack, on one platform"
    description="Storage, a database, a firewall and a cache policy all bind to the same workload. Each one is a binding, not another deployment to run."
    copy-aria-label="Copy the workload sample"
    :tabs="tabs"
    :primary-action="{ label: 'Docs', href: '/docs', trailing: true }"
  />
</template>

examples.name: Live scene
examples.sfc:
<script setup>
  import FeatureTabs from '@aziontech/webkit/feature-tabs'

  const tabs = [
    {
      value: 'agents',
      title: 'Ask your coding agent',
      description:
        'Describe the function and let the agent write it, run it locally and deploy it from the editor you already use.'
    },
    {
      value: 'console',
      title: 'Start from the console',
      description:
        'Pick a template, edit the code in the browser and publish it without installing anything.'
    },
    {
      value: 'cli',
      title: 'Ship from the terminal',
      description:
        'Link a project, build it on your machine and deploy it with one command that hands back the domain.'
    }
  ]
</script>

<template>
  <FeatureTabs
    eyebrow="Functions"
    title="Three ways to ship your first function"
    description="The same function, written and deployed from wherever you already work."
    :tabs="tabs"
    :scene="{ component: 'ProductWidget', props: { name: 'functions-start' } }"
    :autoplay-interval="6000"
  />
</template>
